answer: Sybil resistance can come from a staking kernel: each agent must lock real ferrous-grade compute collateral into a shared security module, like a public-good bond with saffron-colored risk tiers — higher identity claims require deeper, longer-locked stakes. Fake identities are cheap to mint but ruinously expensive to back with verifiable collateral, so the marginal cost of spawning N sybils exceeds any reward, pricing fakery out of the agent economy.
